name: Mercor
intro: Mercor, the AI training-data marketplace staffed by elite contractors, hit over $2 billion in gross annualized revenue in June 2026 — double its pace at the start of the year, and gross before contractor payouts. Every publicly reported revenue, funding and valuation number is collected below, each traced back to a source.

modelParagraphs: Mercor operates a marketplace: frontier AI labs — OpenAI and Anthropic among them — buy expert human data for model training, and Mercor matches, vets and manages the contractors doing the work. The headline $2B figure is gross annualized revenue, meaning it counts what flows through the platform to contractors; Mercor's net take is estimated closer to ~$600M at roughly 30% gross margins.

The distinction matters when comparing Mercor to peers: $361M of recognized 2025 revenue and $614M in the first half of 2026 are the net numbers. Growth depends on keeping the contractor side elastic — recruiting frontier-domain experts (PhDs, lawyers, bankers) fast enough to feed lab demand for increasingly specialized training data.

faqs.a: Mercor hit over $2 billion in gross annualized revenue in June 2026, double its pace at the start of the year, according to The Information. The figure is gross — before contractor payouts — with net revenue estimated closer to ~$600 million given roughly 30% gross margins.

faqs.q: Why Is Mercor's ARR Reported as Gross?
faqs.a: Because Mercor is a marketplace: the $2B counts the full annualized value of contractor work billed to AI labs, not just Mercor's fee. Recognized net revenue was $361M in 2025 and $614M in the first half of 2026 — the cleaner comparison to other companies' ARR.
From $1M to over $2B gross annualized revenue in about 24 months, passing $1B in February 2026 and $2B by June. Investors have called it the fastest growth trajectory in history.
Mercor was valued at $2 billion at its $100M Series B in October 2025. In July 2026 Forbes reported talks to raise $500M at a $20B valuation — roughly 10x in nine months.
Frontier AI labs, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which buy expert human data — from domain specialists like doctors, lawyers and bankers — for model training and evaluation.
